title: Quantitative phenotypic screens of Aspergillus niger mutants in solid and liquid culture
author: Cairns, Zheng, et al.

steps.title: Inoculate liquid cultures
steps.instruction: Prepare 100 mL Erlenmeyer flasks with 20 mL minimal medium (MM) supplemented with doxycycline at 0, 0.2, 2, or 20 µg mL⁻¹; wash all glassware with distilled water before sterilization; ensure all flasks are identical in design; seal with sterilized cotton plugs; add 100 µL of a 2 × 10⁸ spores mL⁻¹ suspension to achieve a final density of 1 × 10⁶ spores mL⁻¹; incubate at 30 °C, 220 rpm in the dark for 72 h.

substeps.instruction: Wash all glassware with distilled water prior to sterilization to remove detergent residues.
Prepare flasks with 20 mL MM and the required doxycycline concentration.
Add 100 µL of 2 × 10⁸ spores mL⁻¹ suspension to each flask (final 1 × 10⁶ spores mL⁻¹).
Seal flasks uniformly with sterilized cotton plugs.
Incubate at 30 °C, 220 rpm, dark, for 72 h.

steps.title: Capture images of culture
steps.instruction: Decant each culture into a clean 50 mL Falcon tube and invert gently several times to separate biomass; transfer 5–10 mL of the suspension into a 25 mL petri dish; image at ~10–20× magnification (captures ~3 mm pellets); acquire >10 pellets per culture if pelleted forms are present; include a ruler image at the same magnification to define µm/pixel; optionally shake the dish or use a sterile pipette tip to separate touching structures; if biomass is very dense, dilute 1:1 with MM or distilled water before imaging.

substeps.instruction: Decant culture into 50 mL Falcon tube and invert gently.
Pour 5–10 mL into a 25 mL petri dish.
Capture images at 10–20× magnification.
Ensure >10 pellets are captured per culture when pellets are present.
Capture a ruler image at the same magnification for scale.
If structures touch, gently shake the dish or separate with a sterile pipette tip.
If biomass is too dense, dilute 1:1 with MM or distilled water before imaging.

steps.title: Organize images and set MPD parameters
steps.instruction: Create a folder for each culture containing all its images; launch MPD via ImageJ (Plugins > MPD); select the input folder and specify an output folder; indicate whether images are light‑on‑dark or dark‑on‑light; define the resolution (µm/pixel) by measuring a known length (e.g., ruler) with ImageJ’s straight‑line tool and using Analyze > Set Scale; set thresholds for dispersed versus pellet structures (default dispersed ≥500 µm²); set a minimal cut‑off to discard artefacts (default <95 µm²); run the MPD analysis.

substeps.instruction: Generate a directory for each culture’s images.
Open ImageJ and choose Plugins > MPD.
Select the input directory and create an output directory.
Specify image background polarity (light‑on‑dark or vice versa).
Define µm/pixel resolution: measure a known length with the straight‑line tool, then use Analyze > Set Scale.
Set thresholds: dispersed structures ≥500 µm²; artefacts <95 µm² (or adjust as needed).
Run MPD analysis.

steps.title: Quality control and visualize data
steps.instruction: Inspect the MPD‑generated quality‑control images; omit any poor calls (e.g., missed pellet boundaries) using their index numbers; compile the MPD output (diameter, area, aspect ratio, solidity, morphology number) and display as box‑whisker plots showing average, median, quartiles, and outliers; plot data using standard box‑whisker conventions (e.g., mean as a cross, outliers as circles).

substeps.instruction: Open the quality‑control images produced by MPD.
Identify and exclude inaccurate calls based on index numbers.
Collect MPD output metrics for each culture.
Create box‑whisker plots for pellet metrics (diameter, area, aspect ratio, solidity, morphology number).
Display mean values as crosses and outliers as circles.
